source: paper1_isa_v5.pdf Tables 2-3 and Fig. 7; paper1_isa_supplement_v5.pdf Section S8 (Table S8, Fig. S7)
headline: Zero real-plant evaluations, ~30x budget saving, no better optimum.
v41_claim_retired: The '83% fewer evaluations (5 vs 30)' headline is retired. HGS-only is routed on being NO WORSE THAN CS-BO(30), explicitly not on superiority.

cost_function.RMSE_y: arithmetic mean of the three per-channel RMS errors (n = 3)

field_matched.note: Matches the noise the plant actually sees.

logging_only.note: Its acquisition sits inside the 5-20 ms noise-aware window but does NOT reproduce the dual-channel noise composition of a running line.

protocols.verdict: Matching the identification protocol to the noise the plant actually sees is what turns the twin from useless to competitive. The conclusion FLIPS between the two protocols, so every stored retuning number must carry its protocol tag.

plant_subset.note: The five slow-transport plants plus the fast plant P189, retained as a documented worst case.

seed_structure.note: The HGS family is deterministic given the identified digital twin.

methods.description: Hierarchical grid search on the digital twin only
HGS on the twin, then 5-eval BO on the plant
HGS on the twin, then 10-eval BO on the plant

v41_comparison.note: For orientation only. v4.1 had HGS-only 0.403, HGS+BO(5) 0.342, HGS+BO(10) 0.337 - i.e. few-shot BO appeared to improve on the transfer. Under v5 all three sit at 0.357 and few-shot BO adds no further median gain.

logging_only_results.note: The pooled 180-run CS-BO median of Table 3 is 0.407; 0.419 is the paired-scope value.

win_rates.scope: HGS-only vs CS-BO(30), five slow plants, paired, field-matched
HGS-only transfer under the logging-only protocol

win_rates.detail: beats cold start in every paired run

warm_start.seeded_at: the SysID-mode operating point itself, K_p* = 100 with T_I derived from theta_hat - NOT the digital twin's optimum
warm_start.reason: The retuned optimum sits near K_p* ~ 15, so the seeded neighborhood is roughly seven times too stiff.
warm_start.note: v4.1 said the warm start 'loses its advantage under cascade feedforward'. v5 says it gives no benefit at any budget.

P189_exception.note: Re-identifying P189 at its own best logging period cuts its parameter error from 293% to 64.6% yet DOUBLES the transfer cost and flips the sign of the sim-to-real gap. A low per-plant parameter error is neither necessary nor sufficient for good transfer.

tail_risk.upper_tail_outliers: every upper-tail outlier is the single fast plant P189 under drift
tail_risk.lower_tail_outliers: every lower-tail outlier is the slow plant P049
tail_risk.note: Both tails are essentially method-independent. The worst-case retuning cost is set by plant heterogeneity rather than by the retuning method - the honest ceiling on the digital-twin budget saving.

hgs_budget.accounting: surrogate evaluations, explicitly excluded from real-plant accounting
hgs_budget.wall_time: a few seconds on a GPU, tens of seconds on a multi-core CPU
hgs_budget.transfers: candidate gain LOCATIONS only; the twin's cost values are withheld because they would bias the real-plant surrogate

budget_saving.framing: parity at a fraction of the evaluation budget, not a performance win
budget_saving.per_event: a single identification experiment followed by at most five real-plant retuning evaluations
